# Repository guidance

- This repository contains versioned GitHub Copilot customization artifacts and documentation about their design.
- Treat changes under `.github/` as executable policy: keep roles, tools, delegation, links, and frontmatter explicit and reviewable.
- Use the existing authoring skills under `.github/skills/` when creating or revising customization artifacts; do not duplicate their procedures in every agent.
- Use the Research → Plan → Implement → Review workflow for consequential changes, and require developer approval before each phase handoff.
- RPIR coordinators must apply the shared [agent-question-resolution](skills/agent-question-resolution/SKILL.md) Skill when a material unknown remains after evidence inspection.
- Cite files, symbols, sources, or observed behavior; separate facts from assumptions and state unknowns instead of inventing repository commands or technology choices.
- Keep Plan, Implement, and Review phase reports concise in chat. Prospectively, every new lifecycle artifact uses an exact repository-relative path of `<NNN>-<artifact-type>.md` in `docs/planning/<initiative-slug>/` or `docs/delivery/<work-item-id>-<short-slug>/`, where `NNN` is exactly three ASCII decimal digits and `<artifact-type>` is `research-brief`, `implementation-plan`, `implementation-report`, or `review-report`. Existing unprefixed `research-brief.md` and `implementation-plan.md` records are legacy artifacts: do not rename, amend, or implicitly migrate them, and do not presume that a legacy plan authorizes a durable report. Every completed Research stage must persist exactly one allocated research brief, every completed Plan stage must create or update exactly one exact approved implementation plan, every approved Implement pass must create exactly one immutable implementation report, and every completed evidence-based Review pass must create exactly one immutable review report as specified below.
- Review reports are the prospective fourth artifact class: completed evidence-based Review passes create exactly one `<NNN>-review-report.md` in the exact named plan's same lifecycle folder. Review reports are immutable, non-authorizing evidence and never revise scope, hierarchy, status, acceptance, or implementation authorization.
- Prefer least privilege. Research, planning, and review are read-only by default; the Plan coordinator has a narrowly constrained exception to create or update only its one exact approved lifecycle implementation plan, and implementation receives edit access only for an approved scope.
- Exception: the `Research` coordinator may use its narrowly granted edit capability to create exactly one newly allocated `<NNN>-research-brief.md` under the selected `docs/planning/<initiative-slug>/` or `docs/delivery/<work-item-id>-<short-slug>/` folder at the end of every completed Research stage. This captures evidence and does not approve a Plan handoff; no other file may be written.
- Exception: the `Plan` coordinator may use its narrowly granted edit capability to create exactly one newly allocated `<NNN>-implementation-plan.md`, or update the exact approved prefixed plan path for a material Plan-stage revision, under the selected lifecycle folder at the end of every completed Plan stage. This captures the planning result but does not authorize implementation; no other file may be written.
- Exception: the `Implement` coordinator may use its narrowly granted edit capability, for an approved pass whose exact prefixed plan path is named by the developer, to create exactly one newly allocated `<NNN>-implementation-report.md` in that plan's same lifecycle folder during final reconciliation. The report is immutable execution evidence, is not approval or scope authority, and no other report or file may be written by this exception.
- Exception: the `Review` coordinator may use its narrowly granted edit capability, for a completed evidence-based pass with valid exact inputs, to create exactly one newly allocated `<NNN>-review-report.md` in the exact named plan's same lifecycle folder during final reconciliation. The report is immutable review evidence only; it cannot revise plan scope or hierarchy, mutate completion markers, authorize remediation, or replace approval controls. Rejected input creates no report; a later Review pass creates a new report rather than revising prior evidence.
- Exception: the `Implement` coordinator may update only the named canonical plan's lifecycle `Status` and existing Work Item/Task/Step completion checkboxes during the approved scoped implementation pass; it may not create or update any other persistent artifact or restructure the hierarchy.
- Exception: the `Review` coordinator may conditionally update only the named canonical plan's `Status` field to `Accepted`, after a non-remediation review outcome and explicit developer acceptance; no other plan content may be written.
- Repository terminal commands are denied by default. Only the `Implement` coordinator may execute a guarded command, never a worker, delegate, Research, Plan, Review, or nested agent, and only when the exact developer-named approved canonical plan records the command in its approved-commands section with its literal text, fixed workspace-contained working directory, purpose, expected output or result, known script/network and other effects, required preflight, fresh per-invocation developer approval point, failure disposition, and post-command inspection. Present the unchanged literal command and fixed directory for fresh developer approval on every invocation; Default Approvals remain required and terminal auto-approval must remain disabled. A tool declaration, plan approval, prior approval, approval setting, or this policy text is not command authorization. Tier 1 is limited to an exact recorded local build, test, or script invocation; it must be denied if any command, directory, output, effect, or other record differs, is inferred, or is absent. Tier 2 is a separately approved dependency-installation invocation, never bundled with or substituted for Tier 1, and fails closed unless preflight reviews the existing `package.json`, existing lockfile, `.npmrc`, dependency sources, and install-script policy; manifest/lockfile mutation, unreviewed lifecycle scripts, unsafe sources, or any other deviation is prohibited. All tiers prohibit secrets or secret-bearing environment/configuration, credentials, login/authentication, publishing, deployment, releases/tags, remote mutation, global installation/configuration, external-path writes, shell composition (including chaining, redirection, substitution, aliases, wildcards, or traversal), `npx`, arbitrary script targets, recursive deletion, and safety-control bypass. Use a secret-free context, sanitize command output and execution evidence, and inspect changed, untracked, generated, and declared output artifacts plus the working directory after every command; execution evidence is not by itself validation, readiness, acceptance, or authorization. Native Windows provides no sandbox-containment guarantee; use fixed workspace paths, human review, and approval as the portable controls, with supported-platform sandboxing only as optional defense in depth. The separate cleanup exception remains limited to removal of an exact directory explicitly listed in an approved canonical plan, after confirming before the operation that it is empty and contained within the workspace, with per-invocation developer approval and terminal auto-approval disabled, followed by inspection of the parent path; it excludes recursion, wildcards, traversal, paths outside the workspace, unlisted targets, unrelated commands, and ordinary command-based validation, and this policy alone does not authorize a cleanup target. The only lifecycle-record mutations are the bounded exceptions above. No browser access, hooks, nested subagents, or new persistent workflow artifacts are approved by default. Research may use the validated `web` capability for cited source research. For Microsoft technical tasks, Research and its `Feasibility Investigator` and `Domain Investigator` workers must consider Microsoft Learn first. The configured, organization-approved Microsoft Learn MCP service is available to those roles for its read-only documentation tools; do not use arbitrary MCP servers, write tools, credentials, tracker access, or server-management capability. Report command-based validation as unavailable until an approved command is documented.
- For any newly allocated artifact, inspect only existing files in the same lifecycle folder whose suffix exactly matches the requested artifact type; use `001` when none has a valid prefix, otherwise use one greater than the maximum valid three-digit prefix. Immediately re-inspect that matching-suffix inventory before creating the exact candidate path. Never overwrite an existing path. Stop and use `agent-question-resolution` when the candidate collides, the inventory is malformed or inaccessible, or allocation intent is otherwise materially uncertain; do not guess, select by highest prefix, suffix-only match, recency, or “latest.” Two scans cannot prove that a deleted prefix was never used, so this prospective contract does not claim historical non-reuse and does not authorize deletion or retirement of numbered evidence.
- The exact developer-named repository-relative path is authoritative for lifecycle identity, approval, plan input, report links, handoffs, status mutations, and Review input. A prefix is an allocation identity only; it never selects a current or approved artifact by itself. The implementation plan remains the sole authority for scope, Work Item/Task/Step hierarchy, lifecycle status, and completion markers. Developer approval before Implement, manual handoffs, `send: false`, Review's explicit developer acceptance, Plan-only hierarchy authoring, Implement's existing-checkbox/Status limits, and the bounded terminal/cleanup controls remain unchanged.
- Review persists its report before disposition or acceptance handling. Only a persisted `No remediation required` report followed by explicit developer acceptance may permit the existing conditional `Status: Accepted` mutation; `Remediation required` and `Blocked / clarification required` reports leave status unchanged and cannot authorize remediation. Remediation requires a separately approved Implement pass naming the exact canonical plan and exact source Review-report path.
- Every RPIR coordinator must resolve an agent-discovered material unknown through the shared [agent-question-resolution](skills/agent-question-resolution/SKILL.md) Skill before phase completion or handoff. Omit an **Open questions** section unless the developer has expressly declared a named question intentionally open or unknown; that declaration does not waive resolution of any other material unknown.
- Keep customization files focused, use relative links for repository resources, and validate discovery through VS Code Customizations Diagnostics when practical.

Current RPIR operating rules are owned by repository policy, phase agents, focused lifecycle instructions, and skills—not historical lifecycle records.
